description_full: H World Group Limited develops and operates leased and owned, manachised, and franchised hotels in the People's Republic of China. The company operates hotels under its own brands, such as HanTing Hotel, Ni Hao Hotel, Hi Inn, Elan Hotel, Zleep Hotels, Ibis Hotel, JI Hotel, Orange Hotel, Starway Hotel, Ibis Styles Hotel, Crystal Orange Hotel, IntercityHotel, Grand JI Hotel, Manxin Hotel, Mercure Hotel, Madison Hotel, Novotel Hotel, CitiGO Hotel, MAXX, Joya Hotel, Blossom House, Steigenberger Hotels & Resorts, Jaz in the City, Grand Mercure Hotel, Steigenberger Icons, and Song Hotels. The company was formerly known as Huazhu Group Limited and changed its name to H World Group Limited in June 2022. H World Group Limited was founded in 2005 and is headquartered in Shanghai, the People's Republic of China.
ceo_bio: Mr. Hui  Jin | Chief Executive Officer | Age 47
culture_narrative: Employs approximately 26K people. Revenue per employee of $144K ranks in the bottom quartile among Consumer Cyclical peers, with revenue growing 17%/yr across its filed history. Stock-based compensation of $2K per employee reflects an ownership culture.
financial_summary: H World Group Limited is a large-cap consumer cyclical business with a $15.9B market cap on $3.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +19% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 32% against a 8% cost of capital — a 24-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 20× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 4.4% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 3.4× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 27% operating margin runs 20pp above the Consumer Cyclical median (7%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.

The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.03 across 377 companies in the universe; the top four hold 26% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are roughly flat over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 11% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 32% and a beta of 0.76, it is more defensive than the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.02 vs 5y 0.58), so read it loosely.
About $69.1M trades a day, enough to build a position.
In past sell-offs it fell 35% in the 2020 crash and 51% in the 2022 bear market.
val: The price sits above its blended-model fair value of $34.70 (margin of safety -45%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 25%), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Multiples send mixed signals against Consumer Cyclical peers: cheaper on EV/EBITDA 3.9 vs 10.7, richer on P/E 37.6 vs 18.8 (sector median).

Earnings yields are thin: an EBIT/EV of 3.0% (vs the 8% bar).
The 16 covering analysts target $60.82 on average, 21% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 32% clears the cost of capital of 8.3% by 24pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 1.26).
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.65x.
ROE of 40% is amplified by 5.1x balance-sheet leverage (DuPont), so ROIC is the cleaner read on the business.

hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $1.4B (9% of market cap).
The current ratio of 0.91 means short-term liabilities exceed current assets.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 19.5% over 3 years and 19.0% over 5 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 27%).
Capex runs 2.8x depreciation (31.0% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
own: Insiders own a modest 1.1%, and institutions hold 53%.
It returns 4.4% a year to shareholders (0.7% in buybacks and 4.3% in dividends).
It pays out 159% of earnings, more than it earns, so the dividend is at risk.
people: With about 26,458 employees, each generates about $144K of revenue, 0.4x the Consumer Cyclical median, and revenue has grown 17.5% a year across its filed history.
The company is founder-led, which often keeps management aligned with long-term owners.
